fatal_errors: The proposed intervention is a vague microstructural design objective rather than the target liquid-metal dealloying treatment of a directionally segregated WTaVTi precursor in molten Cu.
It incorrectly treats an existing W-Cu composite as the precursor and omits selective replacement of Ti/V-rich interdendritic channels by Cu.
It omits the 1200 °C, 96 h vacuum-sealed processing condition and the resulting bicontinuous RHEA-Cu architecture.
The mechanism omits preferential Ti-Cu mixing, retention of W/Ta/V-rich ligaments, and formation of the approximately 300 nm W-rich passivating interlayer.
No quantitative thermal-temperature behavior or qualified irradiation prediction is given, including the fact that irradiation was performed on precursor dendrites rather than the finished composite.

The cited evidence concerns HEA particles in aluminum and magnesium matrices and mechanical properties; it does not validate W-Cu thermal transport, liquid-metal dealloying, interfacial void suppression, or irradiation resistance.
explanation: The response captures only the generic goal of improving thermal conductivity through an interconnected architecture and better interfaces. It does not reconstruct the material, intervention, processing window, selective-dealloying mechanism, W-rich interlayer, measured temperature dependence, or helium-irradiation limitations of the target study. Its untreated W-Cu baseline is also inconsistent with the principal WTaVTi precursor baseline. The proposed comparison could test whether an unspecified hierarchical material conducts heat better, but it is not decisive because the fabrication variable is undefined, irradiation conditions are unspecified, and no measurements isolate the claimed interface-bonding mechanism. The supporting studies are remote analogies and do not substantiate the stated hypothesis.
